clue.text: Pizzas — one put on calories eating three-quarter section

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word means one of its letters is dropped, here the final one
put on means added at the end, so the numeral is tacked onto what follows it in the clue
eating is used loosely here to have the calories abbreviation take on the next piece straight after it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for calories
a zone is a section or area
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pizza order where somebody piles on calories by eating most of a slice.
explanation.walkthrough: CAL is followed by three of the four letters of ZONE, and 'one put on' adds I at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Calzoni is the Italian plural of calzone, a folded, stuffed type of pizza.

clue.text: Slum area of Manila

blocks.note: surface reading: a shanty district in the Philippine capital
setter's reading: manila is a stiff brown paper or card, so this is a slum made of that material

explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter forced by the clue's opening position pushes you towards the Philippines; manila card is the stuff of packing boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard city is an area where homeless people sleep in makeshift shelters of boxes, a kind of slum.

clue.text: Spent boxer risks being this

blocks.note: first meaning: money ... has been paid over or disbursed
second meaning: a fighter knocked flat and senseless on the canvas

explanation.walkthrough: Spent reads as an adjective for the tired boxer, but it stands alone as the first meaning; the rest is a cryptic second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both expending money and knocking someone unconscious, as a boxer may be.

clue.text: Approximately name director

blocks.note: or so means approximately, as in ten or so
standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A rough guess at naming a film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane, so his first name stands for a famous film director.

clue.text: Belief that is godly, fashioned around love

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made into a new form
around says the rearranged letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: i.e. is Latin id est, that is
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A godly creed built around love.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideology is a system of ideas or beliefs, as in a political or religious creed.

clue.text: Pupil once abandoned manual

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A former student has thrown away the textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumna is a female former student of a school or college, so a pupil in the past.

clue.text: A country union keeping breadbasket for harvest time

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within

blocks.note: taken as written
the United Nations is a union of countries
breadbasket is slang for the stomach, the tum

explanation.surface: A farming union protects the grain belt in time for harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: Breadbasket suggests a grain-growing region; it is jocular slang for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is the season when crops are gathered in, the traditional harvest time.

clue.text: Tackled foreign articles — over a thousand

blocks.note: un is French for a, der is German for the
over as in overmuch: too much
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: Someone took on foreign goods worth over a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake a task is to take it on, and tackling a job means the same.

clue.text: A coin is convertible into capital

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so these letters can be recast

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A currency that can be exchanged for capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The money surface makes 'capital' mean funds; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Cried buckets being first exposed to regular lashing

indicators.note: being first tells you the second-named piece goes in front rather than following in clue order

blocks.note: when it buckets down it rains heavily
to cry is to weep

explanation.surface: Someone sobbed their heart out after being whipped again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cried buckets' reads as one idiom for weeping hard, but it splits into two separate pieces, with the buckets placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainswept place is one constantly battered by driving rain, a weather sense of being repeatedly lashed.

clue.text: Cuts weeds

blocks.note: first meaning: to dock is to cut short, as with a tail or wages
second meaning: broad-leaved weeds of the sorrel family

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gardener chopping weeds; in fact the two words are independent meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for trimming or reducing and a plural noun for a common wild plant.

clue.text: Trip over carpet in quiet church, making a row

indicators.note: in a down clue over means above, so the trip word sits on top of the carpet word
in means placed inside the next pair of pieces

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
an outing is a trip
a mat is a small carpet
standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone trips on a church carpet while lining up quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a row' suggests forming a line; row here rhymes with cow and means a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A shouting match is a loud angry argument, and a row is a noisy quarrel.

clue.text: Whistle should be carried by doctor for example

blocks.note: first meaning: a whistle is meant to be sounded with breath, so that is what it should be
second meaning: a doctor is a cooling sea breeze, so anything carried by one is moved along by wind

explanation.walkthrough: The doctor looks like a GP carrying a whistle in a bag; it is a wind, as in the Fremantle Doctor of Western Australia or the Cape Doctor of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle fits both: whistles are sounded by blowing, and things borne along on a breeze are wind-driven.

clue.text: Sparkling Italian lending clout to British-American firm

indicators.note: lending something to another means placing it alongside, so the first piece is put before the rest

blocks.note: to lam is to hit hard, as a clout is
standard abbreviation
United States
company abbreviated

explanation.surface: A lively Italian gives weight to a transatlantic company.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling red wine from Italy, so the adjective-plus-nationality stands for the wine.

clue.text: An army officer before leave becomes close friend

blocks.note: the article
lieutenant abbreviated
old poetic word for before
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: An officer's comrade, about to go on leave, turns into his closest pal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego, literally 'other self', is used for a very intimate and trusted companion.

clue.text: Polish state retaining Mass as seasonal accompaniment

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to something inside

blocks.note: to rub is to polish
standard abbreviation for mass
to utter is to state

explanation.surface: A Polish state keeps up the Mass as part of its festive observance.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes it a nationality next to a religious Mass; it is a verb, and Mass is the physics abbreviation. Polish takes M inside before the state piece follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum butter is a sweet sauce served with Christmas pudding, a festive accompaniment.

clue.text: Scorer shows skill after maiden by Australia

indicators.note: after places the skill word behind the earlier pieces rather than in front of them

blocks.note: M for maiden, as in a cricket scorecard's maiden over
Oz is the informal name for Australia
an art is a skill

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer is impressed by a maiden over bowled for Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes 'Scorer' the person keeping the tally; here it is someone who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart composed, or scored, a vast amount of music, so a scorer in the sense of composer.

clue.text: British Asian's flogged old merchant's china

indicators.note: flogged means beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
the word with its 's, six letters to rearrange
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A British Asian sold off an old trader's porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: China is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate. The merchant is Antonio in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, and his dear friend is Bassanio.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassanio is the friend for whom Antonio, the merchant of Venice, borrows from Shylock.

clue.text: Split in duet regularly affected performance

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at fixed intervals, here every other one starting from the first

blocks.note: first and third letters of the word
camp is theatrical, exaggerated, affected behaviour

explanation.surface: A duo's falling-out shows up in their mannered stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split in duet' suggests a broken partnership; 'Split' alone is the definition, in its slang sense of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, and 'split' is slang for clearing off in a hurry.

clue.text: State voter to start with a line in place of a cross

indicators.note: to start with means only the opening letter of the word before it is taken

blocks.note: Cal. is the short form of California
the first letter
taken as written
RY is railway, a line

explanation.surface: Election instructions telling a voter to draw a line instead of marking an X.
explanation.walkthrough: The ballot paper makes the cross a voting X; it is the cross of the crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvary is the hill outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified.

clue.text: Denigrate rabbit hair

blocks.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length
down is fine soft hair

explanation.surface: Mocking a rabbit's fur.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit is a verb here: British 'rabbit on' means talk endlessly, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk down someone or something is to belittle it, which is what denigrating means.

clue.text: It's crafty folding yellow periodical up in two

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top
in means placed inside the next piece

blocks.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
Roman numeral two, split around the reversed piece
a mag is a magazine

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly folds up a yellow magazine into two.
explanation.walkthrough: Crafty sounds like sly; it means relating to crafts, with the definition reading as a whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Debate is never-ending event

indicators.note: never-ending means the word has no end, so its last letter is lost

blocks.note: to discuss is to debate

explanation.surface: An endless debate.
explanation.walkthrough: Event is an athletics event, not an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus throw is a field event in athletics.

clue.text: Work could make you ultimately suicidal

indicators.note: could make says the following letters can be made into something else by rearranging
ultimately points to the final letter of the word in front of it

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that a job can drive someone to despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The work is Robert Graves's 1934 novel narrated by the Roman emperor Claudius.
explanation.definitionFit: I, Claudius is a famous novel, and a novel is a literary work.

clue.text: Man, following a kiss, accepted proposition

indicators.note: following puts the island piece after the article and the kiss rather than before

blocks.note: taken as written
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man, after a kiss, has his proposal accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement taken as true without proof, an accepted premise.

clue.text: Travellers following a scent

indicators.note: following means the travellers come after the article in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roma are a travelling people

explanation.surface: Wanderers tracking a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell, a scent.

clue.text: Agent raising vital staff

blocks.note: surface reading: an agent recruiting essential employees
setter's reading: the staff of life is bread, and the agent is what makes it rise

explanation.walkthrough: Agent and staff suggest spies or a recruitment firm; 'raising agent' is the baking term and bread is proverbially the staff of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the raising agent that makes bread dough rise by fermentation.

clue.text: Prisoner's social worker pens touching letter

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as in a sheep pen

blocks.note: con is a convict, with the 's
the ant is a social insect and a worker
on means touching, in contact with

explanation.surface: A convict's probation officer writes a moving letter on his behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is not a council employee but an insect from a colony; the prisoner's piece and the insect together do the penning, one either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A consonant is any letter of the alphabet that is not a vowel.

clue.text: Island vineyards hide hollow bark

indicators.note: hollow means emptied out, so the middle of the word is removed and only its shell remains
to hide something is to keep it inside, out of view

blocks.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine
a yap is a sharp bark

explanation.surface: On an island, vineyards conceal a hollow tree's bark.
explanation.walkthrough: Bark suggests trees beside vineyards; it is a dog's yap, emptied of its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island nation, famous among other things for its wines.

clue.text: Prophet, getting nothing wrong, backing excellent horse

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for excellent is read the other way

blocks.note: zero, nought
bad means wrong or wicked
A1 means first-class, written with letters
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A tipster who never got a race wrong, backing a fine horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing and horse paint a racing tipster; backing only turns round AI, and horse is heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Obadiah is a minor prophet of the Old Testament, with the shortest book named after him.
